newsitem.title: NORWAY: Credit Suisse sees rival bid for Fokus.
newsitem.headline: Credit Suisse sees rival bid for Fokus.

text.p: A rival offer for Norway's Fokus Bank can be expected to counter a takeover bid from Sparebankgruppen savings banks, according to Credit Suisse First Boston.
In a market report dated April 15, it suggested the rival bid might come from either a domestic bank or other Nordic banks.
"Nordic banks, notably Den Danske Bank (DDB), have paid high premiums to enter regional retail markets," the report said. "Defensive poison pill options for Fokus are limited."
Fokus Bank, Norway's fourth largest bank, on Monday recommended its shareholders to turn down the 73 crowns per share takeover bid by Sparebankgruppen and did not rule out other bids coming soon.
Fokus says the bid is hostile because Sparebankgruppen, a group of 16 regional savings banks, would carve up the bank's business among its members.

"There is commercial logic in Sparebankgruppen's bid for Fokus but the move is opportunistic and the control premium too low, given rationalisation benefits are likely to be high owing to significant regional overlap," Credit Suisse First Boston said.

"We believe a fair exit price for Fokus is NOK 80-85 per share, and that Sparebankgruppen has pitched its offer too low at NOK 73 per share," it said. "The remaining upside potential and uncertainty leads us, however, to change our recommendation on Fokus from buy to hold."
Sparebankgruppen last Wednesday said it controlled 25.13 percent of the stock in Fokus, which is 80 percent owned by foreign investors.
